Kiln Opening 开窑 · V1.6.1 · for owner sign-off

Interface wireframesNine real game moments, five screen sizes, English and 中文

This is the wireframe set, revised after your sign-off answers of 15 October 2026. Every frame shows a real moment from a game the computer players played on the V1.6.1 rules, seen through one player’s eyes, so it shows only what that player is allowed to see. The counts, choices, costs and error messages are the game’s own, not invented for the picture.

Pick a moment, a screen and a language. The frames respond to clicks: choose a worker and a location, a Contribution card, a Heat-marker side or an Order to complete, and the summary line updates. Click a seat in the top bar to open that player’s board, or open the Game log. Confirm shows what the game would receive; nothing is sent. Go to the wireframes ↓

Owner decisions (15 Oct 2026)

Guiding principle: the screen shows only what a player could see at the physical table. No odds, no previews, no analysis tables. The engine may still work these out for the computer players, but no screen shows them.

  1. D1 · One board area. Every Kiln Player Board lives in one place, the Workshops area. It opens on your own board. Tabs on the board’s top edge, one per other player in their seat colour, switch to their boards, and the Your workshop tab brings you back. Clicking a seat in the top bar opens that player’s board. Other players’ boards show public information only.
  2. D2 · Opponents. The seat chips along the top bar are the public opponent strips. Full boards are one click away through D1.
  3. D3 · Firing. Firing takes over the main column. It shows the step rail, the heat equation (Kiln Die + Contributions = Base Heat; Base Heat + Fire = Global Heat), the kiln with its ceramics, markers and modifiers, the Imperial Kilns and the Fire discard. A fired ceramic shows the Quality you would record on it. The heat ladder and the Heat ledger table are gone.
  4. D4 · Fire cards. No odds and no cards-left counts. The open Fire discard is visible at all times, and that is all the Fire-deck information shown.
  5. D5 · Phones and the log. Phones keep the Table, Kiln, Workshop and Orders tabs. The game log is a dropdown in the top bar at every screen size, not a tab or a section.
  6. D6 · Chinese terms. The glossary terms are approved as they are.
  7. D7 · Second personal space. No “lock” or “unlock” in anything a player reads. The second Form & Decorate or Glaze & Load space is something you add by learning a Tech: “Learn a Workshop Tech to add this space” (习得坯作技艺即添此工位), then “Added by Prepared Clay” (由「练泥」添设).

How the layout works

  1. Fluid grid, no scaled board. Pages reflow with CSS grid, and each component (central board, Shared Kiln, player board, Order display, firing stage) responds to its own width through container queries. Nothing is a fixed 1800px picture shrunk to fit.
  2. 12px floor. No text renders below 12px at 100%. Long rules text opens in a keyboard-reachable disclosure instead of being cut off.
  3. Only what the table shows. Resources, workers, Techs, ceramics, the Kiln Die, revealed Contributions, the turned Fire card, the Fire discard and recorded Quality are on screen. Nothing the physical game would make you work out yourself is worked out for you.
  4. One board area, one decision panel. All Kiln Player Boards share one board area with a tab per player. The right panel opens with a one-row summary of your resources, workers and hand, then the current decision as one form: worker, location, details, a summary sentence, then Clear or Confirm. Place buttons on the central board, the open spaces on your board and clickable kiln spaces are shortcuts into the same form.
  5. Firing is docked, not modal. In the Firing Phase the step rail, the heat equation and the kiln lead the main column. The rest of the table stays live below.
  6. Phones get tabs. Below 900px the screen becomes Table, Kiln, Workshop and Orders with a bottom tab bar, and the decision becomes a one-line strip that opens into a sheet. Workshop is the board area. The app switches tab at the start of Firing, on your Work turn and in the Order Phase. The Game log stays in the top bar.

Not designed yet

  • Final art. Card frames, board illustration, ink-wash backgrounds and the five kiln traditions. Ceramics use the existing neutral cutouts tinted by glaze; colours and type follow the current tokens.
  • Motion (phase 5). Fire reveal, the Quality appearing on each fired ceramic, worker placement and the board tabs switching. Elements carry data-motion hooks, and motion is off under reduced-motion settings.
  • WebGL kiln (phase 6). Fire glow, heat haze, glaze reveal at Quality and Ge crackle growth. It mounts inside the dark kiln body. The DOM kiln underneath stays the accessible source of truth and the fallback.

Not shown in these frames

None of the nine captured moments reaches these states, so they are not designed or shown here and are not part of this sign-off:

  • A Setter’s Mark tile on a Shared Kiln space.
  • The private Test Pieces peek at the top Fire card (step 4) and its bury choice.
  • The private Guild Hall Shifu inspection: the top 2 Techs of a discipline and the secret order for returning them.
  • The Jun choice at step 8 (M4 shows its result in the game log) and the 2-Coin Salvage discard at step 11.

Accessibility and motion hooks

  • Each frame has a polite live region. The caption under the frame shows what a screen reader would announce for that moment (turn changes, reveals, Quality).
  • Quality never relies on colour: every fired ceramic carries its Quality word, or its letter (M, F, S, ×) where space is tight, and the chip’s title gives the ceramic in full.
  • The Game log is a disclosure button in the top bar (aria-expanded, Escape closes it). The board tabs and the seat chips are buttons with pressed states, and focus stays on the control you used.
  • All choices are buttons with pressed states; location cards, kiln spaces and personal spaces are reachable by keyboard. Rules text uses disclosures, not line clamps.
  • data-motion marks every element the motion phase will animate; prefers-reduced-motion turns transitions off.

What came from where

  • Concept C: the two-pane shell, the structured decision form, phase-ordered sections, the 2-player board treatment.
  • Concept B: the kiln-shaped Shared Kiln, Place buttons on locations, clickable kiln spaces.
  • Concept A: the bottom tab bar and one-line action strip on phones, the −1/0/+1 Imperial modifier chips, the labelled 12-step stepper with a queue row, the idle firing summary.
  • Owner decisions (15 Oct 2026): one board area with player tabs and a Your workshop return, seat chips as the opponent strips, the Game log dropdown, “add this space” wording, and no heat ladder, Heat ledger, Fire odds or previews.
